result.title: JevBench: Metamorphic Coherence Testing for Typed Probabilistic Decision Models
result.summary: Typed probabilistic decision models return distributions over specified answers, such as yes or no, a set of options or levels on an ordered scale. We ask whether their probabilities remain coherent when questions about the same input are reworded, negated, combined, given different options or placed in different batches. JevBench tests this coherence without gold labels. Its 50 metamorphic relations each test one law of probability or choice across five dimensions: representation, batch independence, probability measure, logical order and choice-set conditioning. Each test changes the question or batch while keeping the input fixed. Every model receives the same requests, fixed in advance. JevBench-240 contains 12,000 tests across 240 synthetic cases in 12 decision domains. A fixed subset of 1,200 tests, JevBench-mini, closely reproduces the full-suite ranking (Spearman 0.983). Across 21 openly released models, coherence scores range from 56.5 to 83.9. Batch independence holds for most models. Additivity fails broadly, particularly for complements, where the probabilities of a proposition and its negation should sum to one. A uniform reference model ignores the input and scores 89.4 at chance accuracy, exceeding every evaluated model's coherence score. Among decoders, accuracy ranges from 82.4% to 89.2%, while coherence ranges from 64.2 to 83.9. These results show why both measures are needed to assess decision models. JevBench is available as an open-source Python package.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 JevBench：一个无金标签的变形关系测试基准，用 50 条覆盖表示、批次独立性、概率测度、逻辑顺序与选项集条件五个维度的变形关系，检验带类型概率决策模型在改写、否定、组合、更换选项或换批次时输出概率是否自洽。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定输入、只改问法与批次」的一致性检验协议可供核查 LVR 中 latent 推理状态与最终答案是否随表面改写保持稳定、批次组成是否干扰视觉证据使用，但材料完全不涉及视觉或多模态，迁移需人工判断。
